record.paper_title: Remarks on some open problems in phase-field modelling of solidification
record.original_question: What physically consistent evolution equation should be used for the crystal orientation field in coherent polycrystalline matter, where local orientation changes are constrained by crystalline connectivity and positional order? The paper argues that the orientation dynamics should be derived from the evolution of dislocation density rather than from a simple local relaxational law, so the open problem is to formulate a tractable phase-field-compatible orientation equation that respects dislocation motion, elastic interactions, external strain, and interactions with other defects.

evidence.quote: Thus, a consistent equation of motion for the orientation should be based on the evolution of the dislocation density.

However, the development of such an equation is a difficult task, because the motion of dislocations is determined by their complicated elastic interactions, as well as by external strain and interactions with other defects.
Despite intense activity on the phase-field modelling of defects, elasticity, and plasticity (see [42] for a recent overview), such an equation seems at present out of reach.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on phase-field crystal and phase-field dislocation dynamics (e.g., derivations of a Nye-tensor kinematic evolution law from PFC, continuum dislocation dynamics as a conserved-order-parameter phase field theory, and PFDD formulations coupled to micromechanics solvers) has produced partial frameworks linking orientation/density fields to dislocation kinematics. However, no widely accepted, fully tractable orientation-field equation that simultaneously respects coherent-crystal kinematics, elastic dislocation interactions, external strain, and interactions with other defects, suitable as a drop-in replacement for the local relaxational orientation law in polycrystalline phase-field models, has been established. The problem is best regarded as still open, with substantial partial progress.

status_evidence.title: A phase field crystal theory of the kinematics of dislocation lines
status_evidence.snippet: A dislocation density tensor and its kinematic evolution law can be derived from a phase field description of crystal deformations in three dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: kinematic evolution of dislocation density derived within PFC, but not yet packaged as a complete orientation-field equation for polycrystalline phase-field models.

status_evidence.title: Continuum Dislocation Dynamics as a Phase Field Theory with Conserved Order Parameters
status_evidence.snippet: Continuum dislocation dynamics formulated as a phase field theory with conserved order parameters.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing 2024 efforts to cast dislocation-based dynamics in phase-field language, suggesting the unifying problem remains active.

status_evidence.title: Phase field dislocation dynamics formulation coupled with Fourier based micromechanics solver
status_evidence.snippet: PFDD coupled with a micromechanics solver applied to grain boundary–dislocation interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Shows that elastic interactions and defect interactions are still being addressed in separate, specialized frameworks rather than via a unified orientation equation.
